title: Brain Collection Schema — v0.1.5

dead_code_record.description: A single unreferenced code block found by the v4-031 dead code scanner, marked for deletion.

prompt_log.purpose: Rolling 24h conversation log — every prompt and response

LogRecords.description: Array of LogRecord objects stored in the utterances field of conversation_log.json.

LogRecord.description: A single utterance in the conversation log. Four types: user (Skip), assistant (Claude), agent (ConversationLogAgent), service (ConversationLogManagerService).

ch_key.description: Unique key for every utterance. Added by the service before passing to the agent. Not present on records written by Claude or the conversation_log_worker. Required in MongoDB (unique index) but optional in the file.

timestamp_pst.description: PST time with microsecond precision. Unique across all records (B007).

content.description: Verbatim text content of the utterance

jobId.description: Unique job identifier for agent utterances

errorLogFileId.description: Anthropic Files API file_id for the persistent error log

preservePastTime.description: The PST datetime cutoff used for this job

counts.description: Record counts for the job: original in file, retained for client, archived to MongoDB

action.description: Service action performed (e.g. started, called_agent, wrote_file)

outcome.description: Result of the service action (success, failure)

error.required_when: role in (agent, service) and error occurred
error.description: Error details if the action failed

actor.description: Author identifier: Skip, Claude, ConversationLogAgent, or ConversationLogManagerService

prompt_log.title: Prompt Log Protocol
prompt_log.description: Operational protocol for how actors write to prompt_log.json. Loaded by the brain boot process.

write_rules: At session start, read prompt_log.json. Determine next utterance number: max(existing utterances) + 1, or 1 if empty.
After every user prompt: append an utterance with role=user and actor identifying who sent it (e.g. Skip).
After every assistant response: append an utterance with role=assistant and actor identifying who responded (e.g. Claude, GPT).
Write each utterance immediately after it occurs. Do not batch.
If the write fails, continue the conversation. Record failure in application log.
content_rules: Text only — never write binary, base64, or images. Replace with [binary content omitted].
Tool results exceeding 500 chars truncated to first 500 chars + [truncated — N chars].
System-reminder content (tags and their contents) excluded from the log.
Credential redaction is NOT handled by prompt_log. See EPIC-4: Security.
grooming_rules: Claude does not groom, renumber, or delete utterances.
Grooming deletes utterances where timestamp_utc < now_utc - 24h.
Grooming does not renumber remaining utterances.
Groom operation must be idempotent: repeated execution produces identical state.
enforcement: Logging is enforced by Claude Code hooks, not by Claude's discipline.
UserPromptSubmit hook fires on every user message and appends to prompt_log.json.
Stop hook fires when Claude finishes responding and appends Claude's response from the transcript.
Hooks are configured in .claude/settings.json and run automatically outside Claude's control.
actor_rules: Actor is an open vocabulary: Skip, Claude, GPT, or any future participant.
New actors are added as they join the discourse. No controlled vocabulary gate.
timestamp_rules: Every utterance has both timestamp_pst and timestamp_utc.
Grooming decisions use timestamp_utc only. timestamp_pst is for display.
timestamp_utc format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ (microsecond precision per B003)
timestamp_pst format: %-m/%-d/%Y %-H:%M:%S.%f (microsecond precision per B003, no leading zeros)
